authority.alpha_prerequisite: Replace caller-injected installation time with one engine-owned, versioned, fallible host-clock observation; bind its source, trust classification, and anchor into recovery and installed evidence; reject unsafe rollback at durable install/open boundaries; and expose read-only diagnosis without claiming an unauthenticated host clock is absolute trusted time.

current_behavior: At clean baseline 75a1415, public RrdEngine::apply_installation accepts arbitrary at_unix_ms from every caller. The primary CLI reads SystemTime before dispatching even version and no-write plan, panics before the Unix epoch, and forwards the integer as installation authority. The owner-only recovery intent freezes only that integer; the installed record, reopen path, quick verifier, and report carry no source, trust, failure, tolerance, or rollback evidence. open_installed accepts a host clock behind installation. The Linux-only lifecycle proof invokes external kill -INT, proving graceful Unix signal handling rather than abrupt cross-platform process loss. The exact baseline command cargo test -p rrflow-cli --test installed_lifecycle --no-run --locked compiled successfully in 53.90 seconds; no runtime matrix was represented as product proof.
target_behavior: EstateConfiguration format 2 owns bounded clock.maximum_rollback_ms with a strict zero default. RrdEngine obtains a versioned ClockObservation from SystemTime, labels it host_system_time/unverified, converts pre-epoch or unrepresentable values into typed failures, and uses Instant only for elapsed tracing. The first observation is sealed into the install intent and installed record; recovery preserves it. Apply retry, replay, and open compare current observation with that anchor and fail closed beyond policy. Read-only inspect writes nothing, completes structural checks, and reports current, rollback_within_tolerance, rollback_exceeded, or unavailable with exact coordinates; the last two make overall verification failed. Public apply no longer accepts time. CLI version/plan do not read time, quick verify exits nonzero on failed status, and one bounded standard Child::kill/reopen journey is scheduled unchanged on Linux, macOS, and Windows. OpenAPI and SDK/reference projections remain generated from the contract owner.
unchanged_behavior: README, objective, roadmap, and POA&M retain identity, outcome, dependency/status, and deficiency authority; no status closes.

SystemTime remains an unverified observation, not proof of correct UTC. This package does not set the OS clock, contact time services, require network, or claim NTP/NTS, TPM, signed-release time, or platform qualification.

The anchor governs install recovery, replay, verification, and installed open only. Runtime-wide transaction high-water, provider timestamps, attunement leases, session leeway, signed build metadata, and explicit time diagnose/repair plan/apply remain open.

Historical source time, valid time, transaction coordinates, evidence time, and elapsed duration remain distinct. No prompt, thought trace, exploratory reasoning, or unfamiliar semantic idea is forced into a time schema.
Planning remains deterministic and no-write. Verification may observe time but writes no RRFlow/project bytes and invokes no external effect.

Portable user identity and distinct per-machine identity, encrypted backup, typed deletion acknowledgement, external-capability grants, attunement execution, ACL, repair/restore/uninstall, Kubernetes, and signed distributions remain separate packages.
Version 1.0.0, protocol version 1, endpoint operations, Cargo.lock, dependencies, official promotion remote, and ignored .rrflow data do not change.
No release, artifact, tag, push, OS mutation, certificate enrollment, signature, or official promotion is authorized.

sources.title: Rust SystemTime

sources.rejected_assumption: SystemTime proves correct UTC or monotonicity.

sources.title: Rust Instant
sources.retained_behavior: Use Instant only for elapsed tracing/waits.
sources.rejected_assumption: Process-local monotonic time is serializable civil authority.

sources.title: RFC 8633 NTP Best Current Practices
sources.retained_behavior: Make source policy and large correction visible/controlled.
sources.rejected_assumption: One unauthenticated response or silent step is trusted evidence.
